title: The image of decalage representatives equals the embedded spectral page
statement: Let \(C\) be abelian, \(U=(K,F)\) a filtered cochain complex, \(p,q,r\in\mathbb Z\), and \(r\ge2\). Let \(c_r\) and \(m_r\) be respectively the concrete representative class map and the monic right-interval spectral-page embedding [def-sp-filtered-complex-decalage-page-data]. Then \(\operatorname{im}(c_r)=[m_r]\) as subobjects of \(H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Dec}(F)^{1-(q+r-1)}/\operatorname{Dec}(F)^{1-q})\).

source.place: Tag 012K, section-filtered-complex, cycle/boundary and differential formulas; literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, Tag 015X, remark-final-functorial, second filtration. The decalage substitution is an agent derivation of the Tag 012K formulas.

proof.text: At r=2 the left and right intervals coincide. The left-interval representatives are epic onto cycles, and homologyπ is epic, so c_r is epic. The first-page embedding is an isomorphism. Both image subobjects are top.

proof.text: For r>2 put i0=q-r+2, i1=q, i2=q+1, i3=q+r-1. The spectral page is a quotient of H^n(i0,i2) and embeds in H^n(i1,i3). Their composite is the interval map (i0,i2)→(i1,i3): expand cokernelSequenceE.g, kernelSequenceE.f and πE≫ιE, then use toCycles_i and p_fromOpcycles.

proof.text: The representative map onto cycles of the left interval is epic. Its composite with homologyπ and the left-to-right quotient map is c_r, by its defining cycle equation. Endpoint-square naturality transports that quotient map to the spectral-object interval map. Cancel the epic left-interval map in imageSubobject; the image is exactly the monic page embedding.

theorem filteredComplex_decalage_page_image
    (U : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) (p q r : ℤ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    imageSubobject (filteredComplexDecalageRepresentativeClass U p q r hr) =
      Subobject.mk (filteredComplexDecalagePageEmbedding U p q r hr)
